thread:
Rory: During today's UI review I noticed the in-app docs sidecar shows the heading "Runtime labels" but the docs use "Runtime names and aliases". Clicking the sidecar "See docs" link takes users to the top of the page instead of the specific section. Also translators are getting inconsistent strings; some locales still render "labels" vs "names".

Keisha: Nice catch. We should pick one canonical phrase across UI, docs, and translations. I suggest "Runtime name" for short UI labels and "Runtime names and aliases" in explanatory text.

Tom: Agreed. From an implementation perspective the sidecar currently uses relative links like /docs/runtime which our router sometimes ignores hashes for. Use absolute URL + hash to guarantee anchor. Also the sidecar link text "See docs" is ambiguous for screen readers. Prefer explicit link text: "See Runtime names and aliases (opens in new tab)" or sr-only extras.

Iris: Accessibility/UX: if we open docs in a new tab we must add rel="noopener noreferrer" and an aria-label. For tight UI, we can keep "Runtime" visible and append a visually-hidden span: "full docs: Runtime names and aliases, opens in new tab". That keeps the sidecar tidy but accessible.

seo-bot: Note: linking to absolute docs URLs with hash fragments helps search engines and preserves link equity. Consider adding canonical anchors for major terms to avoid duplicate content signals.

Rory: Another nit: table column header in the console reads "Runtime" but the docs header is "Runtime name". Can we standardize the token in DS (design system) as label.short.runtime = "Runtime" and label.long.runtime = "Runtime name" so components can use the right variant?

Keisha: Good approach. I'll add tokens and update Figma components. Also will make sure the help sidecar pulls copy from token keys so copy sweeps don't get out of sync.

Tom: Dev plan: 
1) Update sidecar links to https://docs.redwood.ai/reference/runtime#names-aliases (example).
2) Add target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer and pass aria-label from Link token.
3) Add a small client-side navigation helper on docs that runs: 
   const id = location.hash?.slice(1);
   const el = document.getElementById(id) || document.getElementById('main');
   if (el) { el.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1'); el.scrollIntoView({block: 'start'}); el.focus({preventScroll: true}); }
4) Add an e2e that opens sidecar, activates link, and asserts focus on docs anchor.

Iris: Also check that our sidecar doesn't use aria-hidden on the link text; sometimes designers hide text visually and we accidentally hide it from AT. Use .sr-only patterns that keep text accessible.

Keisha: I'll update the design tokens and add the label.long and label.short keys. I'll also add a tooltip variant for cramped contexts that shows the full long label on hover/focus.

Rory: Docs action: can we add alias anchors for older terminology like #runtime-labels that redirect (via a small note) to #names-aliases? That will preserve existing bookmarks.

docs-bot: Created task #5123: "Harmonize 'Runtime' vs 'Runtime name' across console and docs; fix in-app sidecar links, add alias anchors and a11y fixes" assigned to Keisha, Tom, Iris.

Keisha: I'll own design tokens and Figma updates (ETA 2 days).

Tom: I'll own console link changes + e2e (ETA 3 days).

Iris: I'll do the a11y review and test VO/NVDA after PRs land (ETA after PRs).

Rory: Thanks. After everything lands let's pair and run through keyboard and mobile behaviors. Small follow-up: check translation memory so "labels" doesn't slip back in.

seo-bot: Added canonical anchor suggestion to task #5123 for docs team.
